title: D5 - Object Oriented Programming [COSC 150 1W 26-FA1]
description: [Object-oriented programming] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Object-oriented_programming) (OOP) is a [programming paradigm] (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Programming_paradigm) that is based on the idea of bundling together values and functions into custom objects. It is an important concept that every computer programmer should be familiar with. Search the internet for resources discussing object-oriented programming, and then write a post in this thread with further information about this concept. Your post can consist of any of the following items: * A more detailed description of exactly what OOP is. * A discussion of topics related to OOP. * A discussion of the advantages and disadvantages of OOP. * Comments about the history of OOP, along with examples of languages that do and do not follow this paradigm. * A discussion of how this concept relates to Java. * Anything else that you find relevant to a discussion about OOP. Please post a link to at least one OOP resource that you found online. Discussion Expectations Each week, you will be given a new discussion prompt. You will be expected to respond to this prompt by 11:59 pm CST, Thursday, and will also be asked to reply to at least two of your classmates' posts by 11:59 pm CST, Sunday. You must make an initial post before you are able to view the posts of your peers.

title: D8 - The Java Ecosystem [COSC 150 1W 26-FA1]
description: [java programming on a computer screen] (https://maryville.instructure.com/courses/97939/files/26277283/preview?hidden=1) Java provides collections of methods and tools that can be imported into your Java programs to extend the language's functionality. Java is an open-source language, and anybody is able to create and publish Java packages. There are many talented and dedicated third-party developers who work to create and improve Java packages. You can read about some of the most popular Java packages by reviewing the followings links: * [Top 5 Java libraries in 2020] (https://dev.to/pavel_polivka/top-5-java-libraries-in-2020-1jb0) * [Top 10 Java libraries for saving time] (https://jaxenter.com/top-10-java-libraries-137587.html) Read through these articles and search the web for additional information. * From the reading (listed above), pick TWO packages to discuss. * Use this as a foundation to do further online research on each of the packages you've selected. * In the discussion, explain how each of the packages you selected are used. As the discussion continues we can begin to make comparisons and consider how these packages may be applied. Discussion Expectations Each week, you will be given a new discussion prompt. You will be expected to respond to this prompt by 11:59 pm CST, Thursday, and will also be asked to reply to at least two of your classmates' posts by 11:59 pm CST, Sunday.
